cells.tense: Right now you're running the balance yourself, adding and pulling back by feel, and it's holding. Nothing here is locked in place — you're reading what's in front of you and answering it, and the steadiness that comes out of that reaches the people around you. What the change left standing is safe in your hands.
cells.ask: Offer the fair trade first, out of this balancing act — give the thing before you count what it costs, and let the other side arrive on its own schedule. A middle that keeps itself is the return.
cells.core:
You're the one keeping the blend right, and you do it by feel, not by rule. When something needs more you add it, when something needs less you pull back, and the adjusting runs quietly under everything you do — so the settling isn't a pose you're holding, it's a practice you're living.

That practice is what you can hand forward now. Fairness between you and the people you're in it with doesn't need a ledger — name what you're giving and let the other side land when it lands. Nothing keeps its balance by being guarded; it keeps it by moving.
cells.sheetLine: You keep the balance by feel, and the people around you can tell.
cells.verb: holding steady what the change left standing
cells.place: in the living middle where you keep adjusting the blend

cells.tense: You're braced against a future you can't write in, holding the line so hard it can't breathe. Every adjustment you make answers something that hasn't happened, so the middle you're protecting keeps needing another correction. The holding has become the thing you do.
cells.ask: In this middle that won't sit still, notice one feeling that's actually here and let it be recognized rather than managed — close to it without merging with it. A center that isn't gripping is what you get back.
cells.core:
Calibrating by feel is your real strength — you sense when to add and when to pull back, and the blend stays true without anyone watching the work. That's not a small thing, and it belongs to you. But right now you're holding what the change produced as if the next thing could take it, and the grip is doing what time was supposed to do — hardening what had no reason to harden. Nothing is being held; it's being kept from moving. Every correction is aimed at a morning that hasn't arrived, and the mornings that do arrive get met by a hand that's already tired.

Let one real feeling in, yours or theirs, and stay yourself inside it. The ground holds without you pressing it down.
cells.sheetLine: You're guarding a balance that only stays balanced if you let it move.
cells.verb: holding steady what the change left standing
cells.place: in the living middle where you keep adjusting the blend

cells.tense: You're standing at something that already ended, waiting like it might open again. The adjusting stopped and nothing has moved since, so what the change produced is just sitting there, going quiet. The door isn't the question anymore.
cells.ask: Take one step out of what you actually feel, in this middle, and stand behind that direction. Your own momentum comes back to you, already yours to use.
cells.core:
A hand on a dial is what this looks like when it's working — you feel the room, turn it a little, and the blend stays kind without anyone noticing the work. That hand has gone still. What got left standing when the change finished is still standing, and no one is tending it — a middle that isn't being sensed stops being a middle and becomes a spot you're parked in.

Start from what genuinely moves you, even a little, and defend that one direction. The feeling doesn't have to be big. It has to be yours, and then you act like it.
cells.sheetLine: You stopped adjusting, so the balance can't find you.
cells.verb: holding steady what the change left standing
cells.place: in the living middle where you keep adjusting the blend

cells.tense: You're already adjusting things — you have been — and doing it without knowing it's you doing it. The balance is holding and the hand on it is yours, but the account reads like it happened by itself. The pen is down.
cells.ask: Say one clear thing about how this middle should sit — the shape that serves what it holds — and stand behind it as yours. What you get back is things making sense in your presence.
cells.core:
You read a room and correct for it, and the correction is usually right — that's a real steadiness and it shows in what stays standing around you. You do it so well that no one notices it happening, including the one doing it. What the change produced is being kept, not by accident, by your hand. The keeping is running fine.

The saying-so isn't. Name one way things should sit here and put your authority under it. Not a declaration — just the simple fact of what you're already maintaining. Things fall into place around someone who says what they hold.
cells.sheetLine: You've been holding this steady. Say it was you.
cells.verb: holding steady what the change left standing
cells.place: in the living middle where you keep adjusting the blend
